headline: Adams Point tax increment financing agreement amended, capping housing authority payments at $68,791 a year
summary: The capture rate would rise from 75% to 100% until the district ends in 2052. The economic development director projected about $734,000 in TIF revenue to the city and about 1.2 million dollars in state tax shift benefits. A later order would release the city from a $490,000 commitment to the housing authority through the Affordable Housing Trust Fund. Also approved were a traffic recommendation for Lester B. Orcutt Boulevard and a traffic calming project agreement with the Bicycle Coalition of Maine.
decisions: Approved six citizen committee appointments, unanimously.
Approved moving the Project Canopy Committee into the Sustainability Commission, unanimously.
Approved the traffic committee's recommendation on Lester B. Orcutt Boulevard, unanimously.
Approved the Biddeford Traffic Calming Demonstration Project and the memorandum of understanding with the Bicycle Coalition of Maine, unanimously.
Approved the first amendment to the Adams Point Tax Increment Financing Agreement, 7-1.
Approved naming the executive director of the Biddeford Housing Authority to sign the Adams Point agreement amendment, unanimously.
Approved waiving second reading of the Adams Point amendment, 7-1.
Approved authorizing the council president to sign a letter to the harbor master directing implementation of planning board approval, unanimously.
discussion: Adams Point amendment: Members weighed the $490,000 obligation, the housing benefit, and the cost to taxpayers. Some views opposed changing a deal made by past administrations, while others saw a greater public benefit.

Lester B. Orcutt Boulevard parking: The traffic committee said it struggled to identify the problem and recommended keeping the permanent no-parking restrictions. Members noted busy days, such as weddings, when people walk in the road.

Main Street traffic calming demonstration: Concerns were raised about parking spaces and how bicyclists would share the lane. The traffic committee will review more detailed sketches at its next meeting, next Tuesday, November 24th at 6 p.m.

City communication with residents: Several speakers asked for more notice of meetings, including regular updates and social media posts. A draft council goal calls for a more regular cadence of updates.

Comprehensive plan and audit status: Public speakers asked about the comprehensive plan and the fiscal year 2024 audit. The city manager said the fiscal year 25 bank reconciliations should be done by next Wednesday, and the fiscal year 24 audit is in final review with the vendor.
